subject: Social Studies
stem: A 15th-century poet-saint of the Bhakti movement, born to a Muslim weaver family but revered by both Hindus and Muslims, who composed dohas (couplets) rejecting religious ritualism, idol worship, and caste distinctions in favour of formless devotion to one God, was:
explanation: Kabir's dohas blended Hindu and Islamic mystical ideas, rejecting external ritual in favour of inner devotion — his syncretic teachings are still widely quoted; Tulsidas (Ramcharitmanas) and Surdas (Krishna bhakti poetry) were other major Bhakti-era poets with distinct devotional focuses.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The 8th-century philosopher-saint who propagated Advaita Vedanta (the philosophy of non-dualism, that the individual soul and ultimate reality Brahman are one), and established four monastic centres (mathas) in the four corners of India, was:
explanation: Adi Shankaracharya founded Advaita (non-dualist) Vedanta and established four mathas (Sringeri, Dwarka, Puri, Jyotirmath) — Ramanuja later propounded Vishishtadvaita (qualified non-dualism), a distinct philosophical school within Vedanta.
